title: JSON Mode: Schema-Preserving Fallbacks Across Model-Variant Upgrades (compatibility sweep)
creator: Asha Patel
description: End-to-end evaluation to validate that JSON Mode enforced responses remain schema-adherent during model-variant upgrades and that our schema-preserving fallback rewriter correctly recovers constrained-decoding failures without human intervention. Focus areas: interleaved tool calls, streaming partial emits, KV cache interactions, and routing-induced model fallbacks.
test_plan: Assemble a golden prompt suite representing production patterns: - nested objects, arrays with heterogeneous elements, optional fields, and toolcall markers
Define three model-variant upgrade scenarios: Minor (same-arch, newer weights), Major (seqlen/arch variance), and Cross-quantization (fp16 -> int8 variant)
Run canary traffic mirror with 1% of production requests through compatibility adapter that injects schema gate; collect contract violations and latency distributions
Exercise streaming partial-emits with simulated network interruptions and validate reassembly + constrained-decoder backoff behavior
Inject interleaved toolcall tokens in streaming flow to validate tool-call sentinel preservation and downstream structured parsing
Test schema-preserving rewriter: when strict decoder fails, ensure rewriter performs minimal edits (token-level or field-fill heuristics) and re-validates against schema
Measure observability signals: contract_violation_count, time_to_recover, fallback_rate, increased_p95_latency, and token-overhead for rewrite attempts
Run regression sweep across CPU/GPU serving kernels with KV cache enabled and disabled to detect race conditions or stale-cache signatures that alter structured output
Record reproducible examples for every unique failure mode and link to PRs/bug tickets for follow-up fixes
acceptance_criteria: No schema-violating responses in >= 99.5% of canary traffic across Minor and Cross-quantization scenarios
For Major variant where perfect parity is not expected, automated rewriter recovers valid schema in >= 95% of previously failing cases within 2 retry attempts
Fallback rate (automatic model downgrade) remains below 0.5% of canary requests
Observed median additional latency due to schema enforcement and rewrite attempts is <= 15ms and p95 <= 120ms
All failure classes have a reproducer, a labeled severity, and an assigned follow-up ticket before promotion to production rollout
Telemetry events include contextual artifacts (original model tokens, rewrite diff, schema id, prompt id) persisted to debug log store for at least 30 days
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, SDK, and Observability teams. Consensus to reuse existing streaming harness and extend it with schema gate metrics
2026-03-04: Golden prompt suite drafted (80 prompts) covering nested objects, enums, optional/nullable fields, and 12 toolcall variants. Stored in internal repo: docs/goldens/json-compat-suite

2026-03-06: Prototype schema-preserving rewriter implemented by Research; uses minimal-field-fill and canonical ordering heuristics. Initial microbench shows median 6ms rewrite time on GPU-accelerated path
2026-03-08: Observability event contract defined: contract_violation, rewrite_attempt, rewrite_success, fallback_triggered, schema_revision. Draft sent to telemetry for tagging
2026-03-11: Canary config prepared for 1% mirror traffic. Runtime team to apply traffic-split policy and ensure canary runs on dedicated infra to avoid customer impact
